info.title: Envai AaaS API: execution plane and control plane
info.description:
Contract for the Envai AaaS HTTP surface covering both the execution plane and the control plane. The execution plane serves the Agent Team Protocol (ATP) through the Go gateway: the caller sends messages to a chat, steers or cancels the active turn through small control endpoints, restores a chat from client held context, and reads every agent's activity from one multiplexed SSE stream which is the single source of truth. The chat is the only execution entity: one chat holds one history and hosts many turns, and no parallel run or session lifecycle exists beside it. All endpoints live under the canonical `/api/v1` prefix; legacy `/v1` paths are not aliases and receive no redirect. Event envelopes and per-type payloads are defined once in `events.json` and referenced by the events endpoint through external `$ref`.
The control plane surface served by Laravel is in scope here: workspaces, chats, workspace-scoped chat crons, completion metadata, agent definitions, teams, models, api keys, image operations, signed artifacts and provider webhooks. Control plane responses use the Laravel JsonResource `{data: ...}` wrapper for single resources and collections, except the provider webhook which answers a bare `{status: ok}` and the model catalogs which answer a top-level `{object, data, defaults}` object. Since 1.1.0 the image operations are reserved to authenticated api keys. Since 1.2.0 the workspace files api exposes the workspace fake filesystem (wiki, skills and `MEMORY.md` are plain files under it) through the control plane.
 Contract3 is selected with X-Envai-Contract-Version: 3. Canonical execution routes include /atp/v3 and never downgrade. Old execution mutation routes return 426. Legacy event reads are finite historical snapshots, not live subscriptions. Successful negotiated responses acknowledge the selected version; clients must validate before hydration.
 Since 3.1.0 resource ownership is project based: a company owns projects and a  project owns api keys, agent definitions, teams, workspaces, chats and media. Two principals exist: a human  first-party cookie session with CSRF protection for identity, tenancy and key management, and a project api  key bearer with typed claims for resource work and paid operations. Human requests on root project collections  name the project with X-Envai-Project-Id; a project key derives its project from the credential and a differing  header is rejected. Key creation, listing and revocation are human-session only, and every paid operation  requires a project key. Company usage, project usage and project logs are UTC date-bounded and paginated, and  money is reported per currency as exact decimal strings with unknown costs kept separate, never mixed or  zero-filled. Deleting a company, project, workspace or chat cuts access at once and answers with a durable  cleanup intent whose state stays observable until content removal is confirmed.

post.description: Authenticated native system input. Idle chats wake in a new turn. Busy chats queue until the active turn terminates. Identical event_id retries return the same receipt with duplicate=true; changed content returns 409. Optional origin_turn_id must be known when supplied; omission allows the first notification in an owned chat. strict_model true requires the configured root model at wake admission, and a strict origin cannot be downgraded. Receipts and deduplication are process-local and may be lost on restart or eviction. Never blindly retry an uncertain paid operation after state loss.

post.description: Workflow consumers must require the delegated_job_lifecycle capability before relying on complete-job terminal semantics. Origin and target chats must belong to the authenticated project and the same workspace. Target team is resolved from its existing chat binding. Execution and completion delivery are native Envai operations; the origin turn can finish independently. task_id identifies the complete delegated job; receipt turn_id identifies only its initial target coordinator turn. If that turn delegates detached children, its terminal does not complete the job. Envai waits for the coordinator terminal and all pending children in each cohort, then batches their results into one target synthesis turn. A synthesis that delegates more children starts another cohort. Only a coordinator turn with no pending children or results finalizes the origin task and its integral output. Use origin task.completed or origin GET task terminal status as the phase outcome. Task output is the full final job output, and optional result_turn_id identifies its final coordinator turn. A new delegation whose origin_turn_id belongs to a delegated job can attach only to its currently active coordinator turn; a past coordinator turn is rejected with 422. Exact duplicates still replay their receipt. Keep target-chat SSE open through job terminal for tools and submit their results to that target chat; tool events are not forwarded to origin. Optional notify_origin defaults to true. With the delegation_notify_origin capability, false suppresses only automatic origin delivery and model wake; origin task events, GET, final output and result_turn_id remain available, and target child cohorts and synthesis are unchanged. Omitted and explicit true are equivalent for idempotency; changing the effective boolean for the same event_id returns 409. Optional strict_model defaults to false; true rejects an unavailable configured target root model before admission with 422 strict_model_unavailable and persists the policy through coordinator synthesis turns. Root agent.started.model reports the requested selection; agent.done.requested_model identifies that selection and optional agent.done.model preserves the last provider-reported model, including aliases. An active target chat returns 409. Deduplication is process-local.

post.summary: Start a native job without a parent turn
post.description: Starts a system-input coordinator in this project workflow chat. No origin turn or user message is required. The receipt turn_id identifies initial admission only. Observe task.completed or read task status for final output and result_turn_id after all detached child cohorts and synthesis finish. Client tools stay on this chat SSE stream. No automatic notification wakes another chat. Same request_id and payload replay the receipt while resident; changed payload conflicts. Restart or eviction makes status and deduplication unknown, never evidence that work was not executed. A busy chat returns 409.

post.summary: Send a message and start a turn
post.description: Sends a user message to the chat. The message opens a turn: the gateway resolves the team from `chat.team_id` and starts the orchestrator loop, and the turn is identified by the orchestrator completion id `cmpl_<ulid>` returned as `turn_id`. The server emits `turn.started` with the message as the turn input. The request is rejected with 409 when a turn is already in progress for the chat, with 503 `server_error`/`gateway_draining` while the gateway is draining, and with 404 when the chat does not exist.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream with one `data:` line per event, JSON encoded. Attach with `after=<seq>` to receive retained events strictly after that sequence number. In the current implementation the replay window is bounded and in memory; eviction or restart discards events, resets sequence to 1 and exposes no epoch or cursor-expired signal. Within a resident runtime, positive sequence numbers are monotonic and continuous across turns, including chat.extension placeholders for extension-only events. A wire-only `ping` with `seq: 0` is emitted periodically to keep proxies and load balancers from closing the idle stream. Each `data:` line is one Agent Team Protocol event envelope; `type` discriminates `data`, and the envelope and every per-type payload are defined in `events.json`.

post.description: Stops the active turn and emits `turn.cancelled`. In flight subagents are cancelled through context propagation. The request is rejected with 409 when no turn is in progress for the chat.

post.summary: Record guidance for the active turn
post.description: Validates that a turn is active and records guidance by echoing `turn.steered`. `target_agent_id` is optional and targets the orchestrator when omitted. In the current alpha implementation the text is not injected into the running LLM loop.

Resolves a client tool call (`agent.tool.request`) with the client output. The body carries `call_id` and `output` (required; `output` is the double-encoded JSON string of the client tool contract) and `is_error` (optional, default false). Resolution is at most once by `call_id` while the turn remains active; the broker and its tombstones are discarded at the terminal event. It is not transparently retry-safe because duplicates do not return the original success response. A duplicate while the turn is active answers 409 `tool_already_resolved`, a late output after the timeout answers 409 `tool_timed_out`; after the terminal event the same `call_id` answers 404, as does an unknown `call_id` or one belonging to a different chat, without leaking existence. Success answers 204 No Content and echoes `agent.tool.result` on the stream.

error.message: Tool call already resolved.

post.description: Copies the conversation context of the source chat into a destination chat created beforehand through the control plane. The gateway validates that the destination chat exists, belongs to the same workspace and project and carries no history and no active turn; violations answer 422. The request is rejected with 409 when a turn is in progress for the source chat. After a successful fork the two chats evolve independently.

409.description: A turn is in progress for this chat

error.message: A turn is in progress for this chat.
The destination chat is not valid for forking.

post.summary: Restore a chat from client held context
post.description: Rebuilds the orchestrator from the `orchestrator_context` supplied in the body: the compacted context first, followed by orchestrator assistant messages. Restore is the client driven rehydration path; the gateway can hydrate chats automatically from persisted context when it is available and readable. Loading is fail-open on DB/JSON errors and persistence is asynchronous best-effort, so the restored in-memory context is not a durability acknowledgement. The request is rejected with 409 when a turn is in progress for the chat and with 404 when the chat does not exist. Restore replaces the in-memory context, schedules persistence and does not open a turn, so `turn_id` answers null.

200.description: Chat restored from the supplied context

409.description: A turn is already in progress for this chat

error.message: A turn is already in progress for this chat.
The orchestrator context is not valid.

get.description: Returns protocol metadata and positively advertised names. The current alpha response is not exhaustive and a feature name may advertise an endpoint/event surface without proving the full intended semantics. The delegated_job_lifecycle feature explicitly guarantees the documented cross-team job boundary, cohort synthesis and final task output semantics. Workflows relying on these semantics must require that feature in addition to cross_team_delegation. The delegation_notify_origin feature allows optional notification suppression without changing final-job results. These additive features do not change contract version 3.

X-Envai-Extensions.description: Present only when native-tasks-v1 was accepted

get.description: Returns the current status of the API including timestamp and environment info

Public endpoint serving the JSON Web Key Set of the control plane. It publishes every Ed25519 signing key, active and retired, with its `kid` (`sig_<ulid>`), so tokens signed before a rotation keep verifying. No authentication.

post.description: Creates a workspace with id `wsp_<ulid>` owned by the project named by the project header (or derived from a key credential). The workspace owns the wiki, skills and `MEMORY.md` state and does not own a team. Teams are selected per chat at chat creation.

get.description: Lists the workspaces of the project.
A workspace outside the caller project scope answers 404 without confirming existence.

put.description: Updates the workspace configuration. The workspace does not own a team, so no team field is accepted here. The team is selected at chat creation through `team_id`.

delete.description: Deletes the workspace and its chats: access is cut at once, open subscriptions close and the returned cleanup intent stays pending and observable until the wiki, skills, memory, attachments, sources and storage prefixes are removed. Accounting rows are never removed.

post.description: Registers a project-scoped client tool with id `twl_<ulid>`. The tool belongs to the project named by `X-Envai-Project-Id` or derived from a project key credential, and becomes visible to an agent only when its name is in `agent_definitions.external_tools_enabled`. `name` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,254}$`, be unique per project, and not be a reserved platform tool name (`read`, `list`, `stat`, `write`, `execute`, `wiki_read`, `wiki_ls`, `wiki_write`, `skill_read`, `skill_list`, `skill_write`, `exa_search`, `exa_contents`, `calculator`, `convert_units`, `delegate_task`, `set_chat_title`, `cron`). `set_chat_title` is a built-in `server` tool available only to the orchestrator, never a `client` tool. The native `cron` tool is not registered here; it is enabled per agent through `tools_enabled` and derived permissions. `parameters` must be a JSON Schema with root type `object`; `timeout_seconds` defaults to 120 and is capped at 600.

get.summary: List the client tools of the project
get.description: Lists the client tools registered on the project.
Returns a client tool of the project, by name.

put.description: Updates a client tool. Only `description`, `parameters` and `timeout_seconds` are updatable; `name`, `kind` and `project_id` are prohibited.

delete.description: Removes the client tool from the project registry.

post.summary: Create a chat inside a workspace
post.description: Creates a chat with id `cht_<ulid>` inside the workspace. The chat selects the team through a mandatory `team_id`. `chats.team_id` is a required 31-character `team_<ulid>` reference with a foreign key to `teams`; chat creation validates that the team exists and belongs to the same project as the workspace, 422 otherwise. Omitting `team_id` is rejected with 422.

get.description: A chat outside the caller project scope answers 404 without confirming existence.

put.description: Updates only the server-managed `title`. `team_id`, `workspace_id`, `project_id` and ownership fields are prohibited with 422: the team, workspace and project of a chat are immutable.

delete.description: Deletes the chat: access is cut at once and the returned cleanup intent stays pending and observable until the conversation context, attachments and content are removed. Completion metadata, usage and cost accounting are retained; the content is not.

get.summary: List completion metadata of a chat
get.description:
Lists the metadata-only completion records of a chat, newest first. Results are paginated with `per_page` (default 15, maximum 100) and can be filtered by `status`, `model_orchestrator` and the `started_at` range (`from` and `to`, inclusive, ISO 8601). Records never include message content.
 Omitted or explicit2 selector reads the truthful numeric legacy representation; any unrepresentable item rejects the entire selected page with426. Contract3 exposes nullable current costs and immutable terminal metadata.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Omitted, invalid or non-positive values resolve to page 1.

get.description: Returns the metadata-only record of a single completion of the chat. Omitted or explicit2 selector reads the truthful numeric legacy representation; any unrepresentable item rejects the entire selected page with426. Contract3 exposes nullable current costs and immutable terminal metadata.

get.summary: List chat crons of a workspace
get.description: Lists non-cancelled schedules for the project resolved from the workspace path. An authorized human session or project API key can manage schedules within that project. If `X-Envai-Project-Id` is supplied, it must match the workspace project. The project key, turn and call that originated a schedule are immutable; the current control actor does not become its origin. Public responses omit origin key, turn and call identifiers. Schedule creation has no public endpoint and is limited to the native cron tool during an active project-key- backed turn; a human session cannot start paid work. Results are ordered by creation time and id and can be filtered by `origin_chat_id` and `status` (`active` or `completed`).

parameters.name: origin_chat_id
parameters.description: Only return crons whose origin chat has this id

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return crons with this scheduling status

get.description: Returns one non-cancelled schedule scoped to the project resolved from the workspace path. An authorized human session or project API key may read it; a supplied `X-Envai-Project-Id` must match the workspace project. The original project key, turn and call remain immutable provenance and are not replaced by the principal controlling this request. The public resource omits origin key, turn and call identifiers.

patch.description: Updates the prompt and future scheduling of an active schedule in the project resolved from the workspace path. Only occurrences not yet materialized follow the new settings; existing occurrences keep their immutable snapshots. Origin chat, team, project-key/turn/call attribution, `created_at` and `max_until` are immutable; counters are not reset, and `repeat_count` cannot drop below `scheduled_count`. The human session or project key controlling this request is not the origin actor and cannot reassign it. A supplied `X-Envai-Project-Id` must match the workspace project. Returns 409 when the schedule is not active.

delete.description: Cancels a schedule in the project resolved from the workspace path, fencing occurrences that are not yet admitted. An already admitted turn is not cancelled. The human session or project key controlling this request is distinct from the immutable project-key/turn/call attribution that originated the schedule; this operation does not reassign that origin. A supplied `X-Envai-Project-Id` must match the workspace project. The public resource omits origin key, turn and call identifiers.

get.summary: Read a workspace file or directory
get.description: Reads a single workspace file or directory through the fake filesystem api. Files answer the descriptor plus `content`, directories answer the descriptor plus alphabetically sorted `entries` (at most 500). The root `/` is allowed only here and lists the top level entries (`MEMORY.md`, `wiki`, `skills`). A missing file answers 404 with type `file_not_found`; a missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

post.description: Creates a file at the given absolute workspace-relative path, creating missing parent directories. The response is the 201 descriptor without `content`. An existing file or directory at the path answers 409 with type `file_conflict`. Content must be non empty, valid UTF-8, at most 1048576 bytes and at most 1000 lines; `/MEMORY.md` is additionally capped at 12000 characters. The root `/` and the protected `/wiki` and `/skills` paths are accepted as existing directories only, so create answers 409 for them. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

put.description: Overwrites the content of an existing file. The response is the 200 descriptor without `content`. A missing file answers 404 with type `file_not_found`; targeting a directory answers 409 with type `file_conflict`. Content validation matches create: non empty, valid UTF-8, at most 1048576 bytes and 1000 lines, and 12000 characters for `/MEMORY.md`. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

delete.summary: Delete a workspace file or directory
delete.description: Deletes a file or directory. `recursive=true` deletes a non empty directory, the default is false. The filesystem root and the protected `/wiki` and `/skills` directories cannot be deleted and answer 409 with type `file_conflict`. A missing path answers 404 with type `file_not_found`. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

get.description: Downloads the raw bytes of a file as an attachment. The content type comes from the extension map (markdown, text, pdf, json, csv, html, xml, yaml, image and archive types) with `application/octet-stream` as fallback; `text/*` types get `charset=utf-8` appended by the framework. Targeting a directory answers 409 with type `file_conflict`; a file too large to read answers 422 with type `file_too_large`; a malformed service response answers 422 with type `file_service_error`. Errors answer the standard JSON envelope.

Content-Disposition.description: Always `attachment` with the sanitized file name

post.summary: Convert a markdown or text file to PDF
post.description: Converts a `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` file to PDF and returns the document as an attachment. The conversion itself executes inside the fake filesystem service (pandoc/typst sidecar); authentication, ownership and the per-route throttle remain on this api. Other extensions are rejected with 422 before conversion. A missing file answers 404 with type `file_not_found`; a directory answers 409 with type `file_conflict`; a pdf larger than the configured cap answers 422 with type `file_too_large`. When the file service is unavailable the request answers 503 with type `file_service_unavailable`. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

Content-Disposition.description: Always `attachment` with the base name and `.pdf` extension

post.description: Creates an agent definition with id `agt_<ulid>` owned by the project named by the project header (or derived from a key credential). `mode` is `primary` or `subagent`. The optional `model` must be available in the catalog, `name` must be unique among the project agent definitions and `config` must not contain `max_tokens` at any nesting depth. The four jsonb fields default to empty values when omitted.

get.description: Lists the agent definitions of the project.

put.description: Updates the agent definition with a subset of the creation fields; at least one updatable field is required and `user_id` is prohibited. Field semantics match creation, including the `max_tokens` prohibition on `config` and the catalog availability check on `model`.

delete.description: Deletes the agent definition. The request is rejected with 422 when the agent is the orchestrator of at least one team.

post.description: Creates a team with id `team_<ulid>` owned by the project named by the project header (or derived from a key credential). `orchestrator_id` is required and must reference a primary-mode agent of the same project. The optional `members` array is ordered: `position` is derived from the array order, `role` is nullable and a member cannot be the orchestrator.

get.description: Lists the teams of the project with their members.

put.description: Updates the team with a subset of `name`, `description`, `orchestrator_id` and `members`; at least one updatable field is required. When `members` is present the member list is replaced wholesale, and an empty array clears all members. `user_id` and per-member `position` and `user_id` are prohibited.

delete.description: Deletes the team. A team that still has chats cannot be deleted: the request is rejected with 422 until its chats are reassigned or removed.

get.description: Returns the global LLM model catalog with team entries and the platform defaults per role. LLM entries report `deprecated` and `sunset_at` and carry the informational OpenRouter metadata synchronized from the upstream catalog; models unavailable upstream and models past sunset never appear, deprecated models appear with `deprecated: true`. The catalog itself is platform level and never project scoped; team entries are filtered to the teams of the caller project when the request carries a project context. The optional project header is accepted here and nowhere else changes the catalog rows. The response is a top-level `{object, data, defaults}` object without a data wrapper.

post.description: Creates a long lived api key for the project named by the project header. Key management is human-session only: a project key bearer is rejected with 401 and cannot create, list or revoke keys, and an authorized human manages every key of the project, not only the ones they created. The plaintext token `envai_sk_<ulid><jwt>` appears only in the 201 response and is never persisted or logged: the control plane stores the sha256 hash of the token, the `jti` (`key_<ulid>`), the signing key `kid` (`sig_<ulid>`), nullable `expires_at` and `revoked_at`, nullable creator provenance, `name` and `scopes`. The jwt subject is the project id and it carries no user, role, company, workspace or chat claim.

get.summary: List api keys of the project
get.description: Lists the api keys of the project with their metadata. The plaintext token is never included. Human session only.

delete.description: Revokes the api key: the control plane sets `revoked_at` and adds the `jti` to the Redis denylist so the key stops working immediately even when the jwt has a far future expiry, with no grace window. The row is never deleted. Human session only; a key of another project answers 404 without confirming existence.

post.description: Local and testing only echo endpoint for image generation contract validation. Accepts a multipart upload of up to 4 images and echoes the received prompt, model code and file metadata. No authentication. The request is rate limited to 10 requests per minute. The request is rejected with 404 when the application environment is not `local` or `testing`, and with 422 when the payload or the `model_code` is invalid or unsupported.

Accepts a canonical JSON image generation request and returns 202 with the accepted generation record. Starting paid work requires a project api key: a human session is rejected at the paid boundary and a missing or invalid token answers 401. The generation belongs to the project of the key and records its `api_key_id` as the immutable billing origin at admission, before any provider call. The request is processed asynchronously: the caller tracks progress through `status_url`. The route is throttled to 30 requests per minute (429 when exceeded). With the optional `Idempotency-Key` header a retry with the same payload inside the live generation graph lifetime replays the original generation and origin key without a new dispatch or provider charge, a different payload answers 409, and after expiry or purge the identifier is forgotten. Validation follows the Laravel `GenerateRequest`: required `model`, `prompt` and `webhook_url` (public HTTPS only, no private or reserved addresses), optional input images (`input_images` list up to 10 items, or singular `input_image`), `mask_image` and `objects_image` (each requiring `input_image` and mutually exclusive with `input_images`), `resolution`, `dimensions`, `aspect_ratio`, `format`, `quality`, `model_settings` and `providers`. Model specific validation happens server side: unknown or unsupported models, unsupported quality, resolution or aspect ratio combinations and unsafe input image URLs are rejected with 422 before provider dispatch. Upload records referenced with `upload_id` must belong to the authenticated user and be unexpired: absent, foreign, legacy (no owner) or expired records all answer the same 422 `Upload record not found.` without leaking existence. Referenced uploads are also subject to an aggregate budget of 50 MiB: the `size` of every referenced upload record is summed across all collected inputs (`input_images`, `input_image`, `mask_image` and `objects_image`) and every occurrence counts, so repeating the same `upload_id` in multiple inputs is counted multiple times. Exceeding the budget rejects the request with 422 before any record is created and before provider dispatch. Uploads and generations bind only within one project: a cross-project upload reference is rejected.

get.description: Returns the current lifecycle status of an asynchronous image generation. The `record` path segment is the generation request id `igr_<ulid>`. Requires an authenticated project key or a human session with project context: a missing or invalid token is rejected with 401. Access is scoped to the project: a generation of another project and an unknown id all answer the same 404. `expires_at` is always present and is exactly two hours after creation; `submitted_at` and `completed_at` are null until the corresponding lifecycle phase happens; `result`, `error`, `files`, `price`, `usage`, `cost_usd` and `duration_ms` appear only when available. Per-generation billing metadata lives only inside the live generation graph: at the two-hour purge it is hard-deleted together with the encrypted content and no per-generation log survives; only the project, key, day, currency and cost category aggregate remains.

post.description: Uploads a single image for later use in a generation request through `upload_id`. Starting paid work requires a project api key: a missing or invalid token is rejected with 401, and the route is throttled to 20 requests per minute (429 when exceeded). The file must be an image of type png, jpeg, webp or gif and at most 10240 kilobytes. The record is staged for two hours, belongs to the project of the key and binds to exactly one generation; a bound upload cannot be reused by another generation and a cross-project binding is rejected. It returns id `upl_<ulid>`. A per project disk quota applies: the summed `size` of the project's unexpired uploads cannot exceed the configurable `envai.images.upload_quota_bytes` cap (default 200 MiB), and crossing it answers 422 `The upload storage quota has been exceeded.`. When the quota lock is not available the request answers 422 `Upload temporarily unavailable, retry.`.

get.description: Returns the image model catalog grouped by canonical model. Each entry lists the providers able to serve the model, the price classes with a provider weighted average price and the model settings. Price classes are informational: `average_price` is a provider weighted average, not a guaranteed quote, and a setting applies to the providers listed in its `providers` array, not as a universal constraint. get.summary: Project event logs, filters and retained activity analytics
get.description:
Metadata-only event log of the project, newest first, paginated and time-bounded by the inclusive `from`/`to` UTC window. Filters select events only: `chat_id`, scalar `api_key_id` and scalar `type`, plus the indexed arrays `types[]`, `workspace_ids[]` and `api_key_ids[]`. Values inside one array are ORed, different dimensions are ANDed, and the key dimension matches an event when either its turn key or its actor key is in `api_key_ids[]`. A scalar `type` or `api_key_id` is the single-value form and is rejected when combined with its plural array. `chat_id` stays an additional AND for existing bookmarked links. Arrays accept 1 to 50 distinct non-empty entries (`type` up to 80 characters, ids up to 30) and reject scalar, associative, empty, duplicate, malformed or oversized shapes with 422. Every workspace id must be an active workspace of the project; every key id may be active, expired or revoked. Unknown or foreign ids answer 404 without an existence leak. Entries carry identifiers, sequence, type, timestamp and sanitized metadata only: no prompts, tool output or attachments. Authorized by project like the usage report.
The default view=events returns the paginated entries above. Explicit view=analytics returns full-window metadata aggregates over all retained matching rows, never a page sample; it keeps the scalar `api_key_id` and `chat_id` scope, does not accept `type`, and rejects page, per_page and every filter array. Explicit view=filters returns the complete distinct event type catalog of the project inside the same requested UTC window: no key or workspace names or identifiers, no tokens or content, no top 50 sampling. It rejects type, api_key_id, chat_id, every filter array, page and per_page. The catalog is bounded to 1000 types and fails the whole response with 422 when a window exceeds the cap or contains an empty or oversized type, rather than returning a partial or unfilterable list. Query cost is bounded with a transaction-local statement timeout, and a query failure fails the whole response. Filters and analytics are limited to 90 UTC days even if the general report limit is configured higher. Event retention defaults to 30 days and trace persistence is best-effort; complete retained-row aggregation is not complete execution history. Empty days mean no stored matching events, not proof of no application activity. Tool counts are observed opening events, failures are separate recorded event levels, and durations are measured execution durations, never inferred provider latency or time to first token.

ExcludeAcceptedInvitationsQuery.name: exclude_accepted
ExcludeAcceptedInvitationsQuery.description: Boolean flag serialized as the integer `1` (exclude) or `0` (include), default `0`. When `1`, invitations with the `accepted` status are removed before pagination, so `meta.total`, `meta.last_page`, and page contents describe the filtered collection. Other invitation states are unchanged, and any other value is rejected with `422`.

ProjectLogsView.name: view
ProjectLogsView.description: events is the existing paginated log and the default. analytics aggregates all retained matching rows; page, per_page, type and every filter array must be omitted. filters returns the complete distinct event type catalog of the requested window; type, api_key_id, chat_id, page, per_page and every filter array must be omitted.

ReportFrom.name: from
ReportFrom.description: Inclusive range start as a UTC calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`, default 29 days before `to`. A start after the end or a range beyond the maximum window of 90 days is rejected with 422.

ReportTo.name: to
ReportTo.description: Inclusive range end as a UTC calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`, default today in UTC.

ReportApiKeyId.name: api_key_id
ReportApiKeyId.description: Optional scalar api key id `key_<ulid>` filter for events and analytics. Project logs match the turn key and the actor key of an event. The events view rejects it when `api_key_ids[]` is present and view=filters prohibits it. A project key caller cannot filter by a key of another project; an unknown or foreign key answers 404 without existence leak. Revoked and expired project keys remain filterable.

ReportChatId.name: chat_id
ReportChatId.description: Optional chat id `cht_<ulid>` filter, an additional AND on top of the other event filters. view=filters prohibits it.

ReportType.name: type
ReportType.description: Optional scalar event type filter, for example `agent.tool.request`. The events view rejects it when `types[]` is present; analytics and filters prohibit it.

ReportTypes.name: types[]
ReportTypes.description: Events-only indexed array of event type filters, serialized in form style as repeated `types[]=value` entries. Accepts 1 to 50 distinct non-empty values of at most 80 characters. Values are ORed inside the array and ANDed with the other dimensions. Scalar `types=value`, associative, empty, duplicate, malformed or oversized arrays answer 422, and combining it with scalar `type` answers 422. Prohibited under view=analytics and view=filters.

ReportWorkspaceIds.name: workspace_ids[]
ReportWorkspaceIds.description: Events-only indexed array of workspace filters, serialized in form style as repeated `workspace_ids[]=value` entries. Accepts 1 to 50 distinct non-empty workspace ids of at most 30 characters. Values are ORed inside the array and ANDed with the other dimensions. Every id must identify an active workspace of the project: deleted, unknown or foreign workspaces answer 404 without an existence leak, consistent with workspace deletion and chat access cuts. Scalar, associative, empty, duplicate, malformed or oversized arrays answer 422. Prohibited under view=analytics and view=filters.

ReportApiKeyIds.name: api_key_ids[]
ReportApiKeyIds.description: Events-only indexed array of api key filters, serialized in form style as repeated `api_key_ids[]=value` entries. Accepts 1 to 50 distinct non-empty key ids of at most 30 characters. Values are ORed inside the array and ANDed with the other dimensions; an event matches when either its turn key or its actor key is included. Active, expired and revoked project keys remain filterable, while unknown or foreign keys answer 404 without an existence leak. Scalar, associative, empty, duplicate, malformed or oversized arrays answer 422, and combining it with scalar `api_key_id` answers 422. Prohibited under view=analytics and view=filters.

IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Optional opaque client idempotency key for image generation `POST`, a non-empty printable ASCII string of at most 255 bytes. The live generation graph stores only the sha256 hash of the header, unique per project; the hash is never returned. A matching payload inside the live graph lifetime replays the original generation with its original origin api key without a new provider dispatch or charge, a different payload answers 409, and the guarantee is bounded to the live graph: at expiry or purge the identifier is forgotten and the same header starts a new operation.

EmailVerificationHash.name: hash
EmailVerificationHash.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-1 hash of the email address (40 characters), compared with a constant-time equality check

EmailVerificationExpires.name: expires
EmailVerificationExpires.description: Unix timestamp at which the signed link expires, generated by the native Laravel signed URL with a 60-minute lifetime. An expired link answers 403.

EmailVerificationSignature.name: signature
EmailVerificationSignature.description: Lowercase hexadecimal native Laravel SHA-256 signature of the signed URL (64 characters). It covers the URL path and the full query string, including the `expires` value, and a missing or altered signature answers 403.

strict_model.description: Require the configured root model for the delivery wake. A referenced strict origin cannot be downgraded.

origin_turn_id.description: Optional known resident origin turn. Omit for a new owned notification chat.

error.description: Generic delivery-turn admission failure, if any.

task_id.description: Identifier of the complete delegated job, including child cohorts and synthesis turns.

turn_id.description: Initial target coordinator turn only; its terminal need not be the job outcome.

result_turn_id.description: Final coordinator turn for a delegated or independent job, when available; distinct from receipt turn_id.

delivery_error.description: Native notification failure; the original task output is unchanged.

strict_model.description: Validate configured root before admission and every synthesis. Children retain their model policy.

turn_id.description: Initial coordinator turn only, not the final job outcome.

context.description: Complete workflow context, any non-null JSON value. No truncation or summary.

label.description: Unique exact label, no leading or trailing whitespace or control characters.

task_context.description: Complete task context, any non-null JSON value.

CompletionTerminalSnapshot.description: Immutable metadata-only terminal journal snapshot. Not a replayable ATP envelope and contains no response text. Missing/null for legacy turns. Late provider-cost reconciliation changes current completion usage_cost only.

message.description: Sanitized constant diagnostic; never assistant response text.

chat_cost.description: Frozen chat lifetime USD cost, mirroring chat_usage.cost_usd; null when incomplete or unknown.

v.description: Original immutable terminal wire version; absent only on pre-version journal records.

accepted_protocol_version.description: Version accepted before provider work. A recovered unknown-cost legacy turn can emit a v3 failure without rewriting its original acceptance.

CompletionTerminalSnapshotChatUsage.description: Chat lifetime usage frozen with this terminal snapshot; the ATP Usage fields and nullable legacy USD cost. Omitted by older recovery snapshots.

cost_usd.description: Legacy provider USD cost; null when unknown. Authoritative usage_cost preserves per-currency decimal totals and provenance; no billing.

duration_ms.description: Wall clock duration of the work in milliseconds.

sprite_ms.description: Time spent in the ephemeral Sprite sandbox, 0 when no code tool ran.

sprite_ram_gb_ms.description: Sprite RAM billed in GB-milliseconds, 0 when no code tool ran.

tool_calls.description: Tool invocations counted in the usage window.

error_code.description: Sanitized stable conversion failure code; never a raw provider response or secret. Null when no failure is recorded.

recoverable.description: True only when an automatic technical recovery is durably scheduled and eligible: attempts remain and the source has not completed or been withdrawn. False for initial queued work, healthy running, terminal failures and exhausted retries.

next_retry_at.description: Time of the scheduled automatic technical recovery when recoverable is true; otherwise null. Not an initial work schedule or an operator-repair promise.

message.description: A free-form explanation reported by the managed inbox, not a verified provider fact.

CleanupIntentState.description: Durable content cleanup intent. Access is cut at deletion while the intent stays pending and observable until content removal is confirmed; a failing worker keeps retrying and alerting instead of closing the intent, and a soft-deleted state is never permission to keep content.

status.description: Observable intent state; never reported completed before removal is confirmed.

deadline_at.description: Bounded cleanup deadline; an overrun raises an alert instead of closing the intent

last_error_code.description: Stable sanitized failure code of the latest attempt, null when none

CleanupResult.description: Deletion outcome with the cleanup intents created by the cut

CleanupResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a deletion outcome

UsageMoney.description: Exact decimal amount of one currency; unknown costs are never stored as zero

currency.description: ISO 4217 code; the unknown currency bucket is never mixed into currency totals

amount.description: Exact decimal total as a string

UsageKeyBreakdown.description: Per api key totals of one report day

UsageProjectBreakdown.description: Per project totals of one report day; present only on the company report

UsageMediaTotals.description: Media aggregate totals of one report day or project; no per-generation log survives purge

unknown_currency_observations.description: Priced observations bucketed under the unknown currency marker, kept separate from currency totals

Invocation cost observations are grouped per currency as exact decimals with unknown-cost and not-submitted invocations counted separately; media contributions come from the surviving project, key, day, currency and cost category aggregates.

by_project.description: Per project breakdown on the company report, null on the project report

ProjectLogEntry.description: Metadata-only event log entry. `api_key_id` is the key that started the turn, `actor_api_key_id` the key that performed a control action; both stay null for human events. `agent` and `data` are sanitized to safe metadata keys and never contain prompts, tool output or attachments.

api_key_id.description: Turn key id `key_<ulid>`, null for human or platform events

actor_api_key_id.description: Actor key id `key_<ulid>` of a control action such as cancel, steer or tool output, never rewriting the turn key

turn_id.description: Turn id `cmpl_<ulid>`, null for chat-level events

agent.description: Sanitized agent reference subset (id, role, mode, parent_id, instance_id)

data.description: Sanitized event metadata subset limited to safe keys such as usage, cost, status, duration and identifiers

types.description: Complete sorted distinct event type list of the project inside the requested UTC window.

ProjectEventTypeFilters.description: Type-only filter catalog for the existing log endpoint. It contains the complete distinct type list of the project and window, with no key or workspace names or identifiers, no tokens or content and no top 50 sampling. A window with more than 1000 types or with an empty or oversized type fails the whole response with 422 instead of returning a partial or unfilterable catalog. Reads under the unchanged project log permissions; display names come from the existing api key and workspace session endpoints.

InternalWikiDispatchRequest.description: Internal wiki dispatch envelope. Provenance is mandatory and the actor object carries the proof of the originating work; no user identifier is accepted.

project_id.description: Project id `prj_<ulid>` of the originating work

api_key_id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>` of the originating work

actor.description: Proof of the originating work: `operation_id` with `claim_token`, `fence` and `phase` (`inbox` or `outbox`) for wiki operations, or `turn_id` and `chat_id` with the claim for retrieval; optional `file_id`, `attempt_id` and `attempt_fence` for file attempts.

operation_id.description: Wiki operation id when the actor is a queued operation, empty for retrieval

claim_token.description: Claim token of the operation or turn lease

phase.description: Operation phase; absent for retrieval actors

file_id.description: Source file id of a file attempt

attempt_id.description: Conversion attempt id of a file attempt

attempt_fence.description: Attempt fence of a file attempt

action.description: Domain action name, one of the wiki domain operations (`resolve_source`, `resolve_artifact`, `list_categories`, `get_category_index`, `mutation_status`) or a mutating operation

InternalDispatchResponse.description: `{data: ...}` envelope whose `data` is the action specific domain outcome; failures use the `{error: {code, message}}` envelope with stable lower-case codes.

project_id.description: Project id `prj_<ulid>` of the turn, must match the persisted chat and attachments

api_key_id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>` that starts the turn; no user identifier is accepted

message.description: User message the attachments belong to

idempotency_key.description: Opaque retry key of the turn input, printable ASCII

attachment_ids.description: Attachment ids `att_<ulid>` to resolve; may be empty

InternalAttachmentResolveResource.description: `{data: ...}` envelope with the prepared message, its manifest and the immutable turn provenance.

project_id.description: Project id `prj_<ulid>` echoed from the request and the persisted chat

api_key_id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>` echoed from the request; attribution of the turn

input_id.description: Turn input id of the prepared message

turn_id.description: Turn id `cmpl_<ulid>` reserved for this input

InternalBillingToolLimits.description: Physical execution bound carried only by a Sprite reserve response. model and Exa reservations omit the field entirely. A Sprite configuration whose maximum powered milliseconds is not a positive exact integer above the cleanup grace is unquotable and is refused before any paid provider call.

max_powered_ms.description: Exact powered milliseconds, the minimum of the configured CPU milliseconds maximum and twice the configured RAM GB milliseconds maximum. The cleanup grace is not part of this powered window.

cleanup_grace_ms.description: Fixed milliseconds reserved for the closing call after the powered window.

InternalBillingLlmRates.description: Canonical model rates for an LLM reservation. Each value is an exact decimal string in the billing currency per million tokens or per request. These are rates, never a budget or a total hold.

InternalBillingReservation.description: Successful reserve response data for one source-bound paid step. An LLM reservation carries the canonical per-million rates and a positive token bound. A tool reservation, including Exa and Sprite, carries `max_tokens` 0 and an empty `max_price` object; only a Sprite reservation also carries `tool_limits`. The EUR `max_amount` is the hold, not a customer budget total.

max_amount.description: Exact EUR hold for the quoted maximum

max_tokens.description: LLM completion token bound. Tool reservations return 0 and use unit prices instead.

oneOf.description: Empty object for Exa and Sprite tool reservations

InternalBillingAdmissionRequest.description: Admission provenance for one paid step. The fields name the persisted work; none of them is a user identity and none sets an amount or a price. A project id or key id alone is not proof of the parent work; the control plane resolves the stored project, key, workspace and chat.

api_key_id.description: Active api key id `key_<ulid>` in the same project; never a user.

chat_id.description: Chat id `cht_<ulid>` that owns the paid step.

InternalBillingReserveRequest.description: Reserve payload accepted by the generated Laravel request and the Go client. Only validated fields are present: there is no declared cost, no declared prompt and no raw body escape hatch. The claim token and fence are an optional pair; when one is present the other must be present too.

invocation_id.description: Invocation id `ainv_<ulid>` of the source work.

owner_token.description: Opaque owner token that binds the reservation to one caller.

project_id.description: Project id `prj_<ulid>`; must match the persisted source.

api_key_id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>`; attribution of the paid step, never a user.

chat_id.description: Optional chat id `cht_<ulid>` of the source.

origin_type.description: Source kind bound to the reservation.

origin_id.description: Persisted source id of the declared origin type.

claim_token.description: Optional journal claim token captured from the active lease. The control plane stores it on the reservation; settle and release must repeat the exact pair even after the lease expires or the key is revoked. Provide together with claim_fence or omit both.

claim_fence.description: Optional positive journal fence captured with claim_token; provide only as the same pair.

purpose.description: Optional purpose label of the paid step.

operation.description: Optional tool operation label of the paid step.

InternalBillingSettleRequest.description: Settle payload accepted by the generated Laravel request and the Go client. It repeats the source identity and the claim pair captured at reserve. invocation_id.description: Invocation id `ainv_<ulid>` of the source work.

owner_token.description: Opaque owner token that binds the settlement to one caller.

project_id.description: Project id `prj_<ulid>`; must match the reservation and source.

api_key_id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>`; attribution of the paid step, never a user.

chat_id.description: Optional chat id `cht_<ulid>` of the source.

origin_type.description: Source kind bound to the reservation.

origin_id.description: Persisted source id of the declared origin type.

claim_token.description: Journal claim token captured at reserve, repeated exactly here. A missing or changed pair is rejected with a source mismatch.

claim_fence.description: Positive journal fence captured with claim_token, repeated exactly here.

purpose.description: Optional purpose label of the paid step.

operation.description: Optional tool operation label of the paid step.

observation_id.description: Optional usage cost observation id `ucob_<ulid>` that fixes the source amount.

InternalBillingReleaseRequest.description: Release payload accepted by the generated Laravel request and the Go client. It repeats the source identity and the claim pair captured at reserve. It carries no declared cost, no prompt and no observation: release only returns the unused hold.

invocation_id.description: Invocation id `ainv_<ulid>` of the source work.

owner_token.description: Opaque owner token that binds the release to one caller.

project_id.description: Project id `prj_<ulid>`; must match the reservation and source.

api_key_id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>`; attribution of the paid step, never a user.

chat_id.description: Optional chat id `cht_<ulid>` of the source.

origin_type.description: Source kind bound to the reservation.

origin_id.description: Persisted source id of the declared origin type.

claim_token.description: Journal claim token captured at reserve, repeated exactly here. A missing or changed pair is rejected with a source mismatch.

claim_fence.description: Positive journal fence captured with claim_token, repeated exactly here.

purpose.description: Optional purpose label of the paid step.

operation.description: Optional tool operation label of the paid step.

allowed.description: The context may start the paid step; no reservation or completion is created by the check.

InternalBillingSettleResource.description: Settlement reply: the actual reservation id, the resulting status and the threshold notices. It never carries a fabricated completion or a paid response.

reservation_id.description: Reservation id `bres_<ulid>` echoed from the path.

reservation_id.description: Reservation id `bres_<ulid>` echoed from the path.

status.description: The reservation is released and its unused hold is returned.

InternalBillingNotice.description: Sanitized billing notice. A company notice is amount free and reports exhausted credit; a project or api key notice carries the nonnegative cap amount and the nonnegative public remaining. No provider cost, fee derivation or user identity is exposed.

reset_at.description: Optional end of the current spend period.

InternalBillingError.description: Typed billing service error. `details` is null when no notice applies, otherwise it carries exactly one sanitized notice. It is never a fabricated completion, a raw provider payload or a paid response.

file.description: Native original; MD TXT CSV PDF MP3 MP4 only. The configured per-file native byte limit applies and no conversion, OCR or transcription is scheduled.

Capabilities.description: Event families and optional features advertised by the server. `event_types` is a positive discovery list rather than a parser allowlist, `tool_kinds` lists the supported tool kinds and `features` positively advertised protocol surfaces. A feature name does not by itself prove that every intended semantic is implemented; for example the server advertises `replay` while retention is an in-memory window. `steer` is not advertised: the endpoint records `turn.steered` but does not inject the text into the running LLM loop. Clients remain forward compatible with valid ATP events absent from this response.

families.description: Event families the negotiated surface may emit; task requires native-tasks-v1

CapabilitiesLegacy.description: Event families and optional features advertised by the server. `event_types` is a positive discovery list rather than a parser allowlist, `tool_kinds` lists the supported tool kinds and `features` positively advertised protocol surfaces. A feature name does not by itself prove that every intended semantic is implemented; for example the server advertises `replay` while retention is an in-memory window. `steer` is not advertised: the endpoint records `turn.steered` but does not inject the text into the running LLM loop. Clients remain forward compatible with valid ATP events absent from this response.

ActivityDurationBucket.description: Lower inclusive, upper exclusive. Exactly [0,100), [100,500), [500,1000), [1000,2000), [2000,5000), [5000,10000), [10000,30000), [30000,infinity); null upper_ms means infinity.

ActivityDurationDistribution.description: Only JSON numbers from data.usage.duration_ms in candidate event types, between zero and 9007199254740991 inclusive. Numeric strings, booleans and negative or oversized values are invalid; absent/null is missing. candidate_count = sample_count + missing_count + invalid_count. All summary values are null when sample_count is zero. Zero is a stored value and may also be a producer fallback for invalid timestamps; zero_count is explicit. Tool candidates are agent.tool.complete; turn candidates are turn.completed, turn.failed and turn.cancelled. Client tool waits and agent durations are excluded. Histogram counts sum to sample_count.

ActivityEventTypeGroups.description: Top 50 exact types by count descending, then UTF-8 byte ordering. All omitted groups remain in other_count and daily totals. No row sampling.

ActivityToolGroups.description: Observed openings agent.tool.start and agent.tool.request only, grouped by exact name/kind. Top 50 by count descending then name and kind in UTF-8 byte order, null kind first. Missing, empty, nonstring or oversized names count separately. No inferred running state, deduped lifecycle, or success rate.

coverage.description: The query includes every retained matching row in one database snapshot. Traces can be dropped and purged; configured retention is not guaranteed coverage. Timestamps are null when no rows match.

failures.description: Separate event levels: turn.failed; agent.done with exact failed status; agent.tool.complete or agent.tool.result with strict boolean is_error=true. Unknown or malformed tool flags are unknown, not success. Do not sum levels as unique incidents. is_error is not shell exit-code success.

ProjectActivityAnalytics.description: UTC days are unique, ascending and zero-filled. Counts are safe nonnegative integers. File reads require an observed opening, exact listed tool name, and kind=knowledge. These are file/knowledge-read calls, not unique files, physical I/O, or all managed wiki operations. No raw payload, path, prompt, output or file-name breakdown.
